title: History reference classification
responsibility: Names evidence and archive references and distinguishes source branches from history and internal refs.

inputs.name: sourceArchiveRef.commit
inputs.description: The tested commit id, appended exactly as given to refs/harness/source/ to name the archive ref that keeps the commit reachable after its branch is deleted or rewritten. The shape is not checked here, although the Harness history schemas require a full 40-character lowercase hex hash.

inputs.name: refKind.ref
inputs.description: The full Git reference name to classify, such as refs/heads/main; it is compared exactly with refs/heads/harness-evidence and refs/notes/harness, then matched against the known prefixes in order. A name that matches neither an exact name nor a prefix, for example the short name main, is classified as other.

outputs.name: sourceArchiveRef
outputs.description: The archive ref name: refs/harness/source/ followed by the supplied commit unchanged. The source archive keeps one ref per tested commit, named by its hash, so that commit outlives its branch.

outputs.name: refKind
outputs.description: The kind of the ref, decided from its name alone: 'evidence' only for exactly refs/heads/harness-evidence (checked before the refs/heads/ prefix), 'notes' for refs/notes/, 'archive' for refs/harness/source/, 'internal' for refs/harness/ names outside the source archive, 'tag' for refs/tags/, 'remote' for refs/remotes/, 'source' for refs/heads/ names other than the evidence branch, and 'other' when no known prefix matches. Only 'source' refs are branches of code; evidence, notes and archive refs are history about code.

outputs.name: historyRefs
outputs.type: { evidence: string; notes: string; archives: string }
outputs.description: The names Harness history uses: evidence is the exact branch refs/heads/harness-evidence, notes is refs/notes/harness, and archives is the pattern refs/harness/source/* that matches the source archive refs, not a single ref. The function takes no input, so every call returns these same values.

outputs.type: { evidence: string; notes: string; archives: string }
